items.title: Horn Shirley — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I was into Horace Silver. You know Horace Silver? I was trying to get into him.

ctx.x: And you were happy that whole period?

Child, it was [unclear] slop. Oh, lord. But see during those times, you know, I always had something going on at the house, a little gig or something. I always had food, and the guys would come over and we‘d . . . and meanwhile, I‘m still trying to get into be-bop. I was into Horace Silver. You know Horace Silver? I was trying to get into him. Art Blakey, now I loved Art Blakey. But I‘d try to get into Horace Silver. After
maybe about three or four years I got into Horace Silver, you know, and that was good. [whispers; unclear] Don‘t do that, okay, that little thing there. I didn‘t mean that; I didn‘t mean to.
